rendered: The review starts from total global cobalt reserves, taken from a United States Geological Survey report ([1]7 million metric tons[2]). It then applies a conservative yearly mining efficiency of ≈70%[3], and assumes that only a share of the mined cobalt, ≈40%[4], is directed toward battery manufacturing. Applying these factors (reserves, mining efficiency, and battery share) reduces the total to the usable battery-specific cobalt, which the review gives as ≈2 million[5] globally (the recomputed estimate stated in the review).
